FuelEU

FuelEU Maritime

FuelEU Maritime limits how carbon-intensive the energy used by ships can be. The limit tightens every five years. Ships that beat it can bank or pool their surplus. Ships that miss it pay a penalty. It applies alongside the EU ETS, not instead of it.

Draft guide. We're checking this page against official sources before launch. Always confirm with your regulator.

Step 1

Are you in scope?

You're probably in if…

  • You are responsible for ships of 5,000 GT or more carrying cargo or passengers for commercial purposes
  • The ship calls at EU/EEA ports. Covered: 100% of energy on voyages within the EU and at berth, 50% on voyages into or out of the EU

You're probably out if…

  • Ships under 5,000 GT
  • Fishing vessels, warships and non-commercial government ships

Who regulates it: Your administering EU member state, with independent verifiers who check reports and issue the FuelEU Document of Compliance.

Step 2

Your yearly routine

  1. All yearMonitor energy use and fuels under your FuelEU monitoring plan
  2. 31 JanSubmit last year's FuelEU report to your verifier
  3. 31 MarVerification completed and recorded in the FuelEU database
  4. 30 AprRecord banking, borrowing or pooling; final compliance balance
  5. 30 JunPay any penalty; carry the FuelEU Document of Compliance on board

Key facts

Reduction target vs 2020
2% from 2025, 6% from 2030, 14.5% from 2035, rising to 80% by 2050
Penalty
€2,400 per tonne of VLSFO-equivalent energy shortfall, rising 10% for each consecutive year
Flexibility
Bank a surplus, borrow a limited amount from next year (capped at 2% of the limit, paid back with a 10% uplift), or pool ships together
Shore power
Container and passenger ships must use shore power at major EU ports from 2030
Practical tip

Pooling is where the money is. A ship running on biofuel or LNG can carry a surplus that offsets other ships in your fleet, or a partner's, so look at pooling before you pay penalties.
